item.title: Carl Laemelle: The Making of the Movie Business - Part 4: Florence Lawrence: The First Movie Star
item.description: In 1909, most moviegoers could recognize their favorite actors, but they couldn’t name them. The industry made sure of it. The biggest companies, especially those in Thomas Edison’s Motion Picture Patents Company, refused to put actors’ names in credits or advertising. To them, performers were interchangeable parts in a machine. item.description: There is no magic weight loss pill. Or is there?
